facts.text: The Golden Record was deployed at Interstellar Space (Beyond Heliopause) during Voyager Interstellar Mission in 1977.
facts.source: NASA Golden Record Project (Sagan, Drake et al. 1977)

facts.text: A 12-inch gold-plated copper phonograph record enclosed in a protective aluminum jacket with electroplated uranium-238 clocking. Encodes 115 analog images, greetings in 55 languages, 90 minutes of global music, and natural sounds of Earth.
facts.source: NASA Golden Record Project (Sagan, Drake et al. 1977)

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the deep-space environment.
Pioneered universal interstellar communication protocols, using the 21-centimeter hydrogen hyperfine spin transition and 14 galactic pulsar frequencies as a cosmic map to locate Earth.
Status: Preserved as an eternal time capsule drifting into deep space.
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration in deep space.
